claims: Issue #666 reports nineteen upper bounds beyond the n <= 324 corpus, each the exact rational side in its certificate's header rounded upward at 12 decimal places: s(464) <= 21.988813022694, below Francisco Couzo's certificate of 14 October, and, at 509, 555, 603, 654, 706, 760, 817, 875, 935, 998, 1061, 1128, 1196, 1266, 1339, 1413, 1489 and 1568, a side below the integer ceil(sqrt n).

The issue states that check.py (standard library, exact rational arithmetic) accepts all 19 certificates and that the printed poses pass the same test at 80 digits, with least clearances between 1e-35 and 2e-11, and that no checker outside the author's has run on them. It credits the staircase-rectangle and four-block method of Arslanov, Mustafin and Shangitbayev (Electron. J. Combin. 28(4), P4.22, 2021) and, at 464, a six-square patch from the author's n = 422 construction. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
